    • addPlayer

      public void addPlayer(int clientID, String name, int figure, boolean ready)
      Adds a new player to the internal player mappings and the chat recipient list, excluding the local client. If the player is already present in the recipient box, they won't be added again.
      Parameters:
      clientID - the unique ID of the client to add
      name - the player's display name (optional, must not be blank)
      figure - the ID of the figure (robot) associated with this player
      ready - whether the player is marked as ready

    • displayHandCards

      public void displayHandCards(List<String> cardNames)
      Displays the player's hand cards in the user interface.

      This method performs the following:

      • Checks whether any cards are available.
      • Clears and initializes the register slots (slots 1–5).
      • Displays the cards in the hand card box.
      • Adds a click event to each card to allow moving it into the register.

    • handleCardSelection

      public void handleCardSelection(int clientID, int register, boolean filled)
      Called when a player selects or deselects a card for their register.

      If the player is the local client and the register is being cleared, this method handles the card removal, including restoring it to the hand if it was not part of a manual or swap-related deselection.

      Parameters:
      clientID - the ID of the player performing the selection
      register - the index of the register slot affected
      filled - whether the register is currently filled (true = added, false = removed)

    • startCountdown

      public void startCountdown()
      Starts a 30-second countdown timer and updates the timer label in the UI.

      The label is updated every second and hidden when the time runs out. Any running timer is stopped before a new one starts.

    • askRebootDirection

      public void askRebootDirection(Consumer<String> callback)
      Displays a dialog allowing the player to choose the reboot direction for their robot after falling off the board.

      The dialog shows four arrow buttons (↑ ↓ ← →), each representing a possible direction. When the player clicks on one of the buttons, the selected direction (as a string: "top", "bottom", "left", "right") is passed to the provided callback.

      Parameters:
      callback - A Consumer that receives the chosen direction as a string.

    • showDrawnDamageCards

      public void showDrawnDamageCards(List<String> cards)
      Displays the damage cards drawn for the player.

      This method is called when the server automatically assigns damage cards to the player. It shows the corresponding card graphics in the hand area.

      Parameters:
      cards - List of damage card names (e.g., ["spam", "worm", "trojan_horse"])

    • promptDamageCardSelection

      public void promptDamageCardSelection(int count, List<String> options, Consumer<List<String>> callback)
      Prompts the player to select a specific number of damage cards from the available options.

      This method clears the current hand card area and displays selectable damage cards. Once the player has selected the required number of cards, the given callback is invoked with the selected cards.

      Parameters:
      count - The number of damage cards the player must select
      options - A list of available damage card identifiers (e.g., "spam", "worm")
      callback - A callback function that receives the list of selected cards once the selection is complete
